paper.title_en: Design and prototyping of a muon veto system for the miniNEREUS detector
paper.abstract_en: NEREUS (NEutrino detection for REactor monitoring Using Scintillator) is a proposed shipping container-style mobile neutrino detector for reactor monitoring, utilizing liquid scintillator as its detection medium. For reactor-monitoring–oriented neutrino detectors operating with a shallow overburden or directly at the surface, the muon-induced background is expected to be the dominant background component. To mitigate this background, a prototype detection system, miniNEREUS, was developed to establish an active muon veto capability. In this work, we present the design and performance of a plastic scintillator muon veto detector (PSMV). The PSMV consists of 28 plastic scintillator (PS) strips, instrumented with optical fibers coupled to 224 silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs). The PS strips are arranged in two layers with a total thickness of 4 cm to discriminate muons from ambient gammas. A high voltage system with hundreds of channels was developed with accuracy better than <math altimg="si57.svg" display="inline" id="d1e702"><mo>±</mo></math>0.01V, which can significantly ensure the gain stability of SiPMs. The corresponding multi-channel data acquisition system was established to read the 224 SiPMs individually, with a self-developed trigger system and an optimized veto algorithm, which gives a light yield of 31.16<math altimg="si57.svg" display="inline" id="d1e711"><mo>±</mo></math>0.01photoelectrons/MeV.
